'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Northern Chad offensive|Northern Chad offensive]]
**The [[Chadian ground forces|Chadian army]] says that 300 rebels have been killed and 150 more arrested during [[military of Chad|military]] operations in northern [[Chad]]. Five soldiers are also killed and 36 others wounded in the operation. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/19/over-300-rebels-five-soldiers-killed-in-northern-chad (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi]], [[COVID-19 lockdown in India]]
*****[[Chief Minister of Delhi|Chief Minister]] [[Arvind Kejriwal]] announces a six-day lockdown in the National Capital Region of [[Delhi]] beginning tonight due to a record 25,462 new cases of [[COVID-19]] reported in the past 24 hours. [https://apnews.com/article/pandemics-health-india-coronavirus-pandemic-new-delhi-194b8356811dadf41c552beedff839a9 (AP)]
****Nationwide, a record 273,810 new cases are reported in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the total number of cases to 15 million. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-news/india-sees-record-surge-of-273-810-covid-19-cases-as-tally-tops-15-million-101618801688756.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] reports a record 634 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 7,013. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/50841328/cambodia-logs-a-further-624-new-covid-19-cases-today-total-now-above-7000/ (''Khmer Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]], [[variants of SARS-CoV-2]]
****Hong Kong announces the suspension of all flights from India, the [[Philippines]], and [[Pakistan]] beginning tomorrow after an unspecified variant was detected in the city. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/hong-kong-bans-flights-india-pakistan-philippines-mutated-covid-14650774 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****South Korea reports its first cases of the B.1.617 [[variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] in nine people who travelled from India. [http://world.kbs.co.kr/service/news_view.htm?lang=e&Seq_Code=160922 (KBS World)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****Greece suspends its planned rollout of the [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|Johnson & Johnson]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] pending a review from the [[European Medicines Agency]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/greece-suspends-rollout-jj-vaccine-covid-19-2021-04-19/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]], [[Lineage B.1.617]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports its first three cases of the B.1.617 [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|variant]] originally detected in India, with two of the three cases linked to travel. [https://www.standard.co.uk/news/uk/indian-acting-astrazeneca-gps-department-of-health-b930554.html (Evening Standard)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovakia]]
****[[Slovakia]] reopens stores, churches, libraries, swimming pools, and zoos. It also resumes services at limited capacity as part of the easing of COVID-19-related restrictions. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/slovakia-opens-shops-and-services-as-lockdown-eases (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Turkey]]
****[[Turkey]] reports a record 341 deaths in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 36,267. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/turkey-reports-55149-new-coronavirus-cases-341-more-deaths-health-ministry-2021-04-19/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]]'s two cities of [[Lautoka]] and [[Nadi]] enter into a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after the country records its first community transmission in 12 months. [https://www.fbcnews.com.fj/news/covid-19/greater-nadi-and-lautoka-area-on-lockdown/ (FBC News)]
****All schools will be closed for the next three weeks due to the lockdown. [https://www.fbcnews.com.fj/news/education/school-holidays-to-begin-from-tomorrow/ (FBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]]
****Australia and New Zealand reopen their borders to tourists from either country for quarantine-free travel. [https://www.news.com.au/travel/travel-advice/flights/transtasman-bubble-corridor-between-australia-and-new-zealand-officially-opens/news-story/5f8b18f043d3a8446b99614ed1d29162 (News.com.au)]
*[[Discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]]
**[[Sebastes schlegelii|Rockfish]] in Fukushima is banned from exports after cesium is detected over the Japanese legal limit, likely caused by the discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Nuclear Plant. This is the first ban since the lifting of ban on all Fukushima fish in February 2020. [https://web.archive.org/web/20210419120553/https://www3.nhk.or.jp/lnews/fukushima/20210419/6050014221.html (NHK)] [https://www.chinadailyhk.com/article/163720 (China Daily)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on politics]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
**British [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] cancels a planned trip to India due to an increase in COVID-19 cases in the country. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-pm-johnson-cancels-trip-india-due-coronavirus-worries-2021-04-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Iran–Saudi Arabia proxy conflict]], [[Iran–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**An Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman confirms a meeting between officials of the two countries and says that [[Iran]] has "always welcomed" dialogue with [[Saudi Arabia]]. Among the topics allegedly discussed in the meeting were the [[Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action|Vienna accord]] and a ceasefire in [[Yemen]], where [[Saudi Arabian-led intervention in Yemen|Saudi Arabia has militarily intervened since 2015]]. Saudi sources declined to comment on the meeting. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-always-welcomes-dialogue-with-riyadh-foreign-ministry-says-2021-04-19/ (Reuters)]
*[[Discharge of radioactive water of the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]], [[Japan–South Korea relations]]
**South Korean fishermen stage a maritime demonstration to protest against the [[Government of Japan|Japanese government]]'s decision to release contaminated water from the destroyed [[Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant]] into the Pacific Ocean. Around 150 fishing vessels take part in the protest. [https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20210419005951315 (Yonhap News Agency)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Death of Brian Sicknick]], [[aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**[[Washington, D.C.]]'s [[chief medical examiner]] announces that [[United States Capitol Police|Capitol Police]] officer Brian Sicknick died of [[natural causes]] but notes that "all that transpired [during the riot] played a role in his condition." [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/04/19/brian-sicknick-died-of-natural-causes-after-capitol-riot-medical-examiner-rules.html (CNBC)]
*[[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|Russian opposition]] leader and activist [[Alexei Navalny]], who has been on a [[hunger strike]] for three weeks, is moved from prison to a hospital, according to the Russian prison service. Meanwhile, [[European Union]] foreign ministers hold a meeting to discuss Navalny's health and warn that Russia will be "held responsible" if anything happens to Navalny. [https://www.dw.com/en/russian-prison-service-transfers-alexei-navalny-to-hospital/a-57248156 (DW)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[President of Cuba|Cuban President]] [[Miguel Díaz-Canel]] is officially named First Secretary of the Communist Party following the resignation of [[Raúl Castro]]. He is the first person not of the Castro family to hold the position since the 1959 [[Cuban Revolution]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-56802129 (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Exploration of Mars]], [[Mars 2020|Mars 2020 mission]]
**[[NASA]]'s [[Ingenuity (helicopter)|''Ingenuity'' helicopter]] successfully performs the first powered flight of a helicopter from the surface of another planet. [https://phys.org/news/2021-04-ingenuity-helicopter-successfully-flew-mars.html (Phys.org)] [https://www.wired.com/story/nasa-lands-ingenuity-the-first-ever-mars-helicopter/ (Wired)]
*[[International Space Station programme]]
**Russian [[Deputy Prime Minister of Russia|Deputy Prime Minister]] [[Yury Borisov]] confirms that Russia will withdraw from the [[International Space Station]] beginning in 2025. [https://www.rt.com/russia/521414-iss-russia-quits-2025/ (RT)]
*The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] scraps [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump]]-era restrictions on fetal tissue research at the [[National Institutes of Health]]. [https://www.sciencemag.org/news/2021/04/biden-administration-scraps-human-fetal-tissue-research-restrictions (''Science'')]
*A research team based at the [[Grand Staircase–Escalante National Monument]] in [[Utah]] announces that the many ''[[Teratophoneus]]'' fossils unearthed at the site provide proof that, contrary to popular belief, ''[[Tyrannosaurus]]'' dinosaurs hunted in packs rather than individually. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/climate-environment/2021/04/19/grand-staircase-tyrannosaur/ (''The Washington Post'')]

'''Sports'''
*[[European Super League|The Super League]]
**[[List of presidents of UEFA|UEFA president]] [[Aleksander Čeferin]] states at a press conference that the [[UEFA]] would begin making "legal assessments" on the following day, and that the organization would look to ban the twelve Super League clubs "as soon as possible", while [[Jesper Møller (DBU)|Jesper Møller]], chairman of the [[Danish Football Association]] and UEFA Executive Committee member, says that he expected the three Super League clubs in the semi-finals of the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]]: [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] and [[Real Madrid CF]], to be expelled from the competition this week. [https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/super-league-uefa-exco-member-says-real-madrid-chelsea-man-city-will-be-removed-from-champions-league-semis/ (CBS Sports)]
**[[European Super League|The Super League]] announces that it is taking legal action to prevent any attempts by UEFA and [[FIFA]] to punish its member clubs and players for taking part in its inaugural season. [https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/super-league-legal-action-uefa-23940753 (Daily Mirror)]
**Protests are held outside [[Elland Road]] stadium as Super League member club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] plays [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. Hundreds of people gathered to protest against Liverpool's involvement in the breakaway league. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-leeds-56805822 (BBC News)]
